messages:
tara_support: FYI customer AcmeHealth reporting sudden throughput drop on their dedicated pool — lots of 429s and multi-second tail latency. Started ~09:10 UTC.
sam_runtime: Can you paste a sample request id / timeframe?
tara_support: request ids: rq_8a2f1c (09:12), rq_8a2f5d (09:17). Short chat w/ customer: they said no config changes.
mike_oncall: Pinging metrics: dashboard shows continuous_batcher.backlog spike at 09:08 and avg_batch_tokens jumped to ~950k. Pool size steady at 2 nodes.
sam_runtime: Huh — autoscaler didn't add nodes. Any autoscale errors in logs?
jess_sre: I see repeated autoscaler reasons: "blocked-by-customer-spendcap" and billing-bot posted a hold at 09:06 (invoice threshold hit).
billing-bot: Automated notice: customer_account AcmeHealth reached soft spend cap; burst capacity suspended. See invoice: https://billing.redwood/acme/INV-2026-03-09
tara_support: So autoscaler wanted to scale but was prevented by spend cap — that explains nodes stuck at 2. Customer had a sudden traffic shift (many small requests) which increased batching inefficiency.
sam_runtime: That matches: continuous batching prefers packing many small requests into full batches; with fewer nodes the scheduler stretched existing micro-batches => larger queueing delays. Max_batch_tokens configured at pool level is 1e6 — with only 2 GPUs it hit per-device token ceiling and caused serializing.
mike_oncall: Repro steps I ran:
```
# replay small-req flood against dedicated pool
for i in {1..500}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/dedicated/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rw-arch-v2","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":128}' &
done
```
Result: tail latency climbs >10s after ~200 concurrent inflight. Logs show scheduler refusing to open new micro-batches due to token_budget pressure.
jess_sre: Interim mitigation options: 1) temporarily lift spend cap / allow burst capacity; 2) lower max_batch_tokens across pool to reduce token ceiling per batch; 3) route AcmeHealth to alternate compatible pool (model-variant with smaller seq len).
tara_support: Customer asked for fast fix. I'll open billing ticket to ask for temporary lift. Also asking if we can do a config tweak we can apply immediately.
sam_runtime: Short-term: set pool.max_batch_tokens=600000 and reduce continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms from 80 -> 50 to favor smaller, faster batches. That reduces packing but improves tail latency. I'll prepare a canary.
mike_oncall: I'll run the change in canary pool now and monitor.
(5m later)
mike_oncall: Applied to canary: saw tail latency drop ~45% within 2 minutes. Continuous_batcher.backlog down. Customer still on blocked pool though.
jess_sre: Billing confirmed: customer agreed to lift soft cap for 1 hour, billing team toggled burst=true at 09:45. Autoscaler immediately scaled to 6 nodes; throughput recovered.
tara_support: Customer confirms 429s stopped and client-side queues draining. They were surprised this was a billing-block interaction — good to know.
sam_runtime: Root cause summary: customer spend cap prevented autoscaler from provisioning burst capacity during sudden small-request spike. Reduced nodes + high max_batch_tokens created inefficient packing and token-ceiling contention, causing serial processing and high tail latency / 429s.
jess_sre: Action items: [ ] Docs note on "spend cap vs autoscale" in support KB (tara) [ ] Add alert when autoscaler transitions show "blocked-by-spendcap" (sam) [ ] Consider dynamic max_batch_tokens heuristic when pool node count below threshold (mike)
tara_support: I'll file the KB now and keep customer updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
